claim_text: A history of kidney stones does not automatically justify restricting dietary calcium or starting a calcium supplement; assessment should distinguish dietary calcium from supplemental calcium and consider stone composition, total intake and individual clinical advice.
health_goal_or_outcome: Avoid inappropriate calcium restriction or supplementation in people with nephrolithiasis history.

population.sex_or_life_stage: Life-stage requirements differ, including pregnancy and older age.
population.health_status: People with previous or recurrent kidney stones.
population.other_context: Stone composition and hypercalciuria status materially affect dietary advice.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Dietary calcium and supplemental calcium salts are not interchangeable in exposure timing or context.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Calcium Health Professional Fact Sheet provides general calcium intake and safety context; stone prevention requires individualized urology/nephrology guidance and current stone-prevention recommendations.
limitations: This claim does not establish that calcium supplements cause or prevent stones in an individual.
Stone type, diet, urine chemistry and supplement timing are not captured by this general claim.
Requires corroboration with current nephrolithiasis guidelines.
